name: NVIDIA Nemotron Labs Dory 1.0 4B
purpose: 4B open language model for general-purpose reasoning on a small footprint.

license.name: OpenMDW-1.1
license.notes: OpenMDW-1.1 text read in the Nemotron 3.5 Lightning repo LICENSE and on openmdw.ai: 'permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to deal in the Model Materials without restriction, including under all copyright, patent, database, and trade secret rights'; conditions are only to keep the agreement and notices when distributing, and termination if you sue over patent or copyright infringement by the materials; 'no restrictions or obligations with respect to ... outputs'. This repo has no LICENSE file; the card tag names openmdw-1.1 with the same link.

architecture.kind: looped (latent-recurrent) normalized GPT with sliding-window and full attention
architecture.recurrent: none (the 20-layer block is looped, not a state-space model)
architecture.attention: interleaved sliding window and full attention; 8 input + 20 shared recurrent + 8 output layers
architecture.why_this_design: NVIDIA: loop count is adjustable per request (compute for accuracy without retraining), fewer output tokens because extra computation happens in latent space, last-loop KV caching so memory does not grow with loops, efficient pre-training natively in NVFP4.

engine_support.notes: An official Q5_K_M GGUF 'for llama.cpp' exists; whether mainline llama.cpp supports the looped layers was not checked.

weaknesses: Numbers for most benchmarks are in a table the fetch tool could not align

tona_fit.reason: Interesting looped architecture (compute scales with loop count), OpenMDW-1.1 (text read) and fits every class, but English-only and unproven against Qwen3.5-4B/9B. Missing looped-layer path is only a blocker.

open_questions: GPQA, IFBench, AA-LCR scores per loop count
Does llama.cpp support the looped architecture?
